review_notes: Read the whole target file (one long cancellation theorem plus two short smoothness lemmas) and compared against sibling Section4 files (IteratesMaterialPrimitive, IteratesTimeProduct, IteratesTime). The smoothness lemmas are short and not duplicative. The only nontrivial repeated machinery is the Fubini-style 'a.e.-in-t split of the fibre integral of a sum, then split the outer interval integral' block, which appears in the target and in IteratesMaterialPrimitive. The pointwise algebra differs between the two uses, so the shared lemma would only cover the plumbing. I did not compile the proposed lemma, and the gain is modest, so confidence is moderate.

findings.problem: The proof does the same fibrewise-additivity and outer-additivity argument as iterate_material_primitive_pairing. First it uses filter_upwards with prod_right_ae and uIoc membership, and rewrites the fibre integral of a sum with integral_add. Then it takes intervalIntegrable_iff.mpr of integral_prod_left for each summand. Finally it rewrites with intervalIntegral.integral_add. IteratesMaterialPrimitive repeats this with three summands, and the same integral_prod_left to intervalIntegrable step occurs in other Section4 files. The Fubini and integrability bookkeeping is therefore re-derived in each proof, which obscures the real content (the pointwise identity f·Mf = g·f + h·f).
findings.proposed_change: Add a small shared lemma in IteratesTime (or a new util file). For F G : ℝ → Vec 2 → ℝ, take hF : Integrable (fun p : AmnrSpace => F p.1 p.2) ((volume.restrict (Set.uIoc 0 T)).prod (volume.restrict unitCube)), and hG likewise. The conclusion is (∫ t in 0..T, ∫ x in unitCube, (F t x + G t x)) = (∫ t in 0..T, ∫ x in unitCube, F t x) + (∫ t in 0..T, ∫ x in unitCube, G t x). Proof sketch: use intervalIntegral.integral_congr_ae_restrict with filter_upwards [hF.prod_right_ae, hG.prod_right_ae] and integral_add on each fibre. Then apply intervalIntegral.integral_add with IntervalIntegrable obtained from intervalIntegrable_iff.mpr hF.integral_prod_left and the same for hG. In the target, state the pointwise identity hpoint as an a.e.-in-t statement, or rewrite the integrand through intervalIntegral.integral_congr_ae_restrict using only hpoint and uIoc_of_le. Then apply the lemma with F := g·f and G := h·f, replacing the hg, hh and integral_add steps and the second filter_upwards block. In iterate_material_primitive_pairing, apply the lemma twice (or a three-term version) to replace lines 59–78 apart from the product-rule rewrite.
findings.benefit: The Fubini plumbing is proved once, and each caller shows only its own pointwise identity. This shortens both proofs and removes a source of divergence. Future cancellation lemmas in this section that split iterated integrals can reuse the helper.
